```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4)
```

This vignette runs the three simeq modules on `simeq_synthetic_panel`, four
fully synthetic survey waves (1998, 2005, 2014 and 2019) with the same
structure as the Portuguese National Health Survey (NHS) data used by
SIMEQ-PT. The data are drawn from simple parametric distributions
(`data-raw/create_synthetic_panel.R`); no survey record is used. **The results
below are illustrative only and are not SIMEQ-PT estimates.** The full
SIMEQ-PT analysis is `analysis/simeq_pt_analysis_v10.qmd` in the source
repository.

To keep the vignette fast it uses two replications, 2,000 sampled entrants a
year and a projection to 2030; SIMEQ-PT uses 50 replications to 2040.

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
library(simeq)
library(dplyr)

panel <- simeq_synthetic_panel
count(panel, year)
```

## Inputs

The 1998 wave is the baseline population, and respondents aged 20-24 in each
wave form the donor pools from which new 20-year-olds are sampled.

```{r inputs}
population_1998 <- panel |>
  filter(year == 1998L) |>
  select(person_id, age, sex, education_level, education_level2, bmi,
         survey_weight, weight, height)

donor_pool <- function(wave) {
  panel |>
    filter(year == wave, age >= 20L, age <= 24L) |>
    select(sex, age, education_level, bmi, survey_weight, weight, height)
}

donor_pools <- list(
  list(from = 1999L, to = 2004L, pool = donor_pool(1998L)),
  list(from = 2005L, to = 2013L, pool = donor_pool(2005L)),
  list(from = 2014L, to = 2018L, pool = donor_pool(2014L)),
  list(from = 2019L, to = 2030L, pool = donor_pool(2019L))
)
```

Mortality uses the bundled Portuguese life table, all-cause relative risks
by BMI category (Global BMI Mortality Collaboration) and a relative risk of
0.981 per year of education (IHME-CHAIN), as in SIMEQ-PT.

```{r mortality}
life_table_raw <- readxl::read_excel(
  system.file("extdata", "prob_dying_qx.xlsx", package = "simeq")
)

# Remaining life expectancy (the YLL reference) from qx at ages 0-100
life_expectancy <- function(qx) {
  lx <- cumprod(c(1, 1 - qx))[seq_along(qx)]
  Lx <- (lx + c(lx[-1], 0)) / 2
  Lx[length(qx)] <- lx[length(qx)] / -log(1 - qx[length(qx)])
  rev(cumsum(rev(Lx))) / lx
}

life_table <- bind_rows(
  transmute(life_table_raw, age = as.integer(age), sex = "men",
            qx = as.numeric(qx_m) / 1000),
  transmute(life_table_raw, age = as.integer(age), sex = "women",
            qx = as.numeric(qx_w) / 1000)
) |>
  mutate(ex = life_expectancy(qx), .by = sex) |>
  filter(age >= 20L, age <= 84L)

ref_life_expectancy <- select(life_table, age, sex, ex)
life_table <- select(life_table, age, sex, qx)

rr_bmi <- tidyr::crossing(
  sex = c("men", "women"),
  tibble::tribble(
    ~bmi_category,   ~rr_bmi,
    "underweight",   1.47,
    "normal_weight", 1.00,
    "overweight",    1.11,
    "obesity_I",     1.44,
    "obesity_II",    1.92,
    "obesity_III",   2.71
  )
)

years_of_education <- c(low = 6, medium = 12, high = 16)
rr_education <- population_1998 |>
  summarise(
    mean_years = weighted.mean(years_of_education[education_level],
                               survey_weight),
    .by = education_level2
  ) |>
  transmute(education_level2, rr_education = 0.981^mean_years)

simeq_validate_life_table(life_table)
simeq_validate_mortality_risks(rr_bmi = rr_bmi, rr_education = rr_education)
```

## Module I: BMI trajectories

BMI change is estimated for each percentile (10th to 90th) of synthetic
cohorts followed between consecutive waves, and education upgrading from
secondary to higher education after entry is estimated the same way.

```{r transitions}
bmi_percentile_model <- simeq_fit_bmi_transition_percentile(
  panel,
  probs = seq(0.1, 0.9, by = 0.1),
  sex_interactions = TRUE,
  life_table = life_table,
  rr_bmi = rr_bmi,
  rr_education = rr_education
)

education_upgrade <- simeq_combine_education_upgrade(list(
  list(from = 1998L, to = 2004L,
       upgrade = simeq_fit_education_upgrade(panel, periods = 1998L)),
  list(from = 2005L, to = 2013L,
       upgrade = simeq_fit_education_upgrade(panel, periods = 2005L)),
  list(from = 2014L, to = NA,
       upgrade = simeq_fit_education_upgrade(panel, periods = 2014L))
))
```

Each year's entrants match the weighted number of 20-year-olds in the
nearest wave.

```{r entrants}
settings <- simeq_settings(
  initial_year = 1998L,
  projection_end_year = 2030L,
  entry_age = 20L,
  max_age = 84L,
  n_simulations = 2L,
  entrant_n_per_year = 100L,
  seed = 2026L
)

entrants_by_wave <- panel |>
  filter(age == 20L) |>
  summarise(entrant_population = sum(survey_weight), .by = c(year, sex)) |>
  rename(wave = year)

entrant_targets <- tidyr::expand_grid(entry_year = 1999:2030,
                                      sex = c("men", "women")) |>
  mutate(wave = case_when(entry_year <= 2004L ~ 1998L,
                          entry_year <= 2013L ~ 2005L,
                          entry_year <= 2018L ~ 2014L,
                          TRUE ~ 2019L)) |>
  left_join(entrants_by_wave, by = c("wave", "sex")) |>
  transmute(entry_year = as.integer(entry_year), sex,
            entrant_population = as.numeric(entrant_population))
```

```{r simulate}
simulation <- simeq_run_simulation(
  population = population_1998,
  settings = settings,
  life_table = life_table,
  rr_bmi = rr_bmi,
  rr_education = rr_education,
  donor_pool = donor_pool(1998L),
  donor_pools = donor_pools,
  entrant_targets = entrant_targets,
  bmi_update_method = "percentile",
  bmi_percentile_model = bmi_percentile_model,
  bmi_period = "by_year",
  education_upgrade = education_upgrade
)
```

Simulated obesity prevalence by sex, compared with the synthetic waves:

```{r obesity}
simulated <- simulation |>
  filter(alive) |>
  summarise(obesity = weighted.mean(bmi >= 30, survey_weight),
            .by = c(simulation, year, sex)) |>
  summarise(obesity = mean(obesity), .by = c(year, sex))

observed <- panel |>
  summarise(obesity = weighted.mean(bmi >= 30, survey_weight),
            .by = c(year, sex))

library(ggplot2)
ggplot(simulated, aes(year, 100 * obesity, colour = sex)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(data = observed, size = 2) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Obesity prevalence (%)", colour = NULL,
       caption = "Lines: simulation; points: synthetic survey waves") +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Module II: health outcomes

```{r module2}
qalys <- simeq_calculate_qalys(simulation_output = simulation,
                               min_age = 20L, max_age = 84L)
head(qalys$by_year)

burden <- simeq_calculate_obesity_burden(
  simulation_output = simulation,
  rr_bmi = rr_bmi,
  ref_life_expectancy = ref_life_expectancy,
  min_age = 20L,
  max_age = 84L
)
head(burden$by_year)
```

## Module III: costs

Direct medical costs attributable to high BMI, using the bundled 2018
Portuguese cost matrix and GBD 2019 relative risks:

```{r module3}
gbd_rr <- read_gbd_bmi_rr()

costs <- calculate_annual_obesity_costs(
  simulation_output = simulation,
  gbd_rr_matrix = gbd_rr,
  costs_dro = obesity_direct_costs_2018(),
  outcome_mapping = obesity_cost_outcome_mapping(),
  exclude_disease_groups = c("obesity_overweight", "depression"),
  years = c(2018L, 2030L),
  exposure = "high_bmi",
  weight_col = "survey_weight"
)

# Thousands of 2018 euros, all included disease groups
summarise(costs$by_year, attributable_cost = sum(total_obesity), .by = year)
```
